name: ZZIPlib
reason: No numeric comparison against any baseline found. Opened and checked: github.com/gdraheim/zziplib (70 stars, COPYING.LIB, no releases listed), raw README.MD, DEVGUIDE.md, TODO and ChangeLog from the develop branch (only grep hits: 'compression based solely on free algorithms provided by zlib', 'ninja should be faster than makefile-build' about the build system, and 'rewrite pagesize/mapoff calculations - this should be faster in itself', a 1.26k-line ChangeLog note with no numbers), and the project site zziplib.sourceforge.net (only 'speed up dat-file development dramatically', about developer workflow). Issue #147 'Faster lookup of entries in large file-count Zip' is a feature request by a user: reading the central directory of a >1M-entry archive costs 'double digit MB' versus about 40MB for regular unzip, an idea for a sorted alternate index with no measurement of zziplib against minizip, libzip or any other library. Two WebSearch queries (zziplib vs minizip/libzip/miniz read speed; zziplib faster/slower benchmark) found no shootout or third-party timing that includes zziplib; only package descriptions calling it 'intentionally lightweight'. The library is a read-only ZIP access layer over zlib, so it is not expected to beat zlib or minizip, and the project makes no speed claim.
